catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction focused exclusively on non-agentic structural, behavioral, domain, and infrastructural software engineering patterns in cas_runner and portal assets.
analysis_limits: Analysis derived from repository directory structure, dependencies, workflow definitions, and key module symbol declarations.
Agentic-specific prompt orchestration and multi-agent workflow interactions were explicitly excluded to preserve boundary fidelity.

system_map.overview: cas_runner is a structured Python-based continuous architecture and governance engine. It utilizes standard layered separation: presentation via CLI, orchestration through FlowRunner, business domain logic via governance models and compliance engines, and infrastructure access through pluggable clients and static documentation generation pipelines.

layers.name: presentation
layers.purpose: Command-line interface entry points, command dispatching, and static dashboard presentation.

layers.name: application
layers.purpose: Workflow coordination, action execution services, and pipeline running.

layers.name: domain
layers.purpose: Core governance entities, state transitions, compliance metrics, and calculation engines.

layers.name: infrastructure
layers.purpose: External provider abstractions, OpenTelemetry telemetry integration, and LLM transport abstractions.

patterns.name: Typed Domain Model Validation via Pydantic
patterns.summary: Use of strongly typed, self-validating data structures to model core governance metrics, actions, and findings.
patterns.intent: Ensure schema integrity, runtime validation, and clear serialization boundaries across internal domain entities.
patterns.context: Continuous governance evaluates disparate project metrics, structural health signals, and compliance findings which require deterministic data contracts.
forces: Dynamic dictionary payloads lead to fragile parsing and silent runtime schema failures.
Manual type-checking bloats core business logic.
patterns.solution: Define explicit schema models using Pydantic BaseModel to encapsulate validation rules, defaults, and serializable domain objects.
implementation_signals: Heavy reliance on Pydantic dataclasses/BaseModel in domain modules.
Domain records defined separately from workflow orchestrators.

evidence.note: Declares declarative data structures defining the domain boundaries of governance assessments.

benefits: Automatic validation prevents invalid states from entering core processing.
Self-documenting domain model with native JSON schema export capabilities.
costs: Tight dependency of domain objects on external validation library.
failure_modes: Validation errors thrown at runtime when external formats drift without migration logic.

patterns.name: Registry-Driven State Transition
patterns.summary: Registry pattern used to decouple state transition rules and governance action handlers from the action execution engine.
patterns.intent: Allow extensible registration and dispatch of architectural state transitions without modifying central dispatch loops.
patterns.context: Governance actions transition through multiple stages (e.g., proposal, verification, convergence, exception handling) requiring flexible rules.
forces: Monolithic conditional branching (`if-elif-else`) becomes fragile and hard to maintain.
Extending actions requires modifying existing control flows.
patterns.solution: Expose a dedicated TransitionRegistry mapping allowed state transitions and handlers, invoked dynamically by the GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: Separation between engine runner and transition definitions.
Explicit registry class managing valid routes or action transitions.

evidence.note: Coordinates lifecycle transitions using an explicit transition registry.

benefits: Open-Closed Principle adherence: new transitions can be registered without altering core evaluation code.
Clear traceability of valid versus invalid state changes.
costs: Requires indirect lookup mechanisms, marginally increasing execution path tracing complexity.
failure_modes: Missing or misregistered transitions leading to unhandled state runtime errors.

patterns.name: Service Facade for Governance Operations
patterns.summary: Coarse-grained service facade encapsulating complex domain engine interactions behind a single application-level interface.
patterns.intent: Provide a simplified, unified entry point for CLI commands and runner flows to execute governance actions.
patterns.context: Executing governance actions requires orchestrating compliance checking, state transitions, model validation, and logging.
forces: Clients should not need to instantiate and wire multiple low-level domain engines directly.
Direct domain coupling in CLI leads to code duplication across commands.
patterns.solution: Provide GovernanceActionService as an orchestration boundary that manages domain engine lifecycles and transactions on behalf of clients.
implementation_signals: A Service class acting as intermediary between CLI/Runner and domain engines.

evidence.note: Encapsulates action resolution, policy coordination, and execution workflows.

benefits: Shields application callers from internal domain complexity.
costs: Can risk becoming a 'God class' if business logic leaks from engines into the service.
failure_modes: Service becoming a pass-through layer with little added value if engines are called in isolation.

patterns.name: Pluggable Infrastructure Adapter with Mock Fallback
patterns.summary: Abstracted client adapters providing uniform interfaces for external I/O integrations alongside in-memory mock implementations for isolated testing.
patterns.intent: Decouple domain logic from remote infrastructure dependencies and enable offline unit/integration testing without network round-trips.
patterns.context: Components require integration with third-party APIs (such as LLM providers or external services) which are slow, rate-limited, and costly during local runs.
forces: Direct coupling to remote API libraries inhibits deterministic automated testing.
Environment drift across development, CI, and production environments.
patterns.solution: Implement standardized provider clients behind uniform call signatures, accompanied by deterministic mock clients fulfilling the same interface contract.
implementation_signals: Parallel implementations: a production wrapper client alongside a dedicated mock client in the same subsystem.

evidence.note: Production concrete adapter wrapping underlying library calls.
Mock test-double adapter implementing identical interface for isolated environments.

benefits: Enables zero-cost, rapid integration testing in CI/CD pipelines.
Isolates vendor dependency changes to single adapter files.
costs: Maintaining fidelity between mock client behaviors and live external client responses.
failure_modes: Mocks drifting from actual API response formats causing tests to pass while production fails.

patterns.name: Pure Functional Evaluation for Health Scoring
patterns.summary: Separating state calculation logic into pure, stateless functions operating over immutable status structures.
patterns.intent: Eliminate side-effects during metric evaluation and simplify verification of composite health indicators.
patterns.context: Continuous architecture dashboards need to calculate health grades and explanatory failure reasons from dynamic repository inputs.
forces: Embedding state and I/O into calculation models makes health assertions difficult to test.
Complex rule combinations create brittle status machines.
patterns.solution: Structure health assessments as pure functions that accept raw metrics and return enum statuses and reason lists without mutating inputs or executing I/O.
implementation_signals: Standalone calculation functions taking metric data and returning structured models.
Absence of class state or instance storage for assessment logic.

evidence.note: Functional evaluation taking metrics and computing pure status enumerations and reason collections.

benefits: Determinism: identical inputs always yield identical health reports.
High testability with minimal setup or teardown fixtures.
costs: Requires the caller to collect and assemble all contextual metrics prior to invocation.
failure_modes: Data starvation if caller omits requisite metrics needed for deep validation.

anti_patterns.name: Static Web Asset Dispersion across Source Trees
symptoms: Minified third-party search and presentation vendor scripts (e.g. lunr, glightbox) checked directly into documentation/portal subdirectories.
Mix of generated site output and source code in tracked directories.
impact: Repo bloat, noisy diffs during updates, security scanning alerts on obfuscated minified scripts, and poor package boundary hygiene.
Increased risk of license non-compliance and out-of-date vendored dependencies.
suggested_remediation: Isolate documentation generation artifacts in ephemeral build caches or use package managers (e.g., npm, pip) to supply documentation theme dependencies.
Ensure built assets (`portal/site/assets/*`) are strictly managed in `.gitignore` rather than committed to source control.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Observability and Tracing
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Integration of OpenTelemetry (opentelemetry-api, opentelemetry-sdk declared in pyproject.toml) throughout execution paths to provide unified telemetry across governance evaluations.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Schema-Driven Artifact Documentation
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Use of static site rendering (MkDocs with Material theme and DrawIO diagramming) coupled to project metadata to publish architecture documentation.

open_questions.question: Does cas_runner persist state transition logs purely to Markdown/JSON files within cas-knowledge/ or is an internal relational/KV datastore planned?
Does FlowRunner operate purely synchronously over pipeline stages, or is async/multithreaded evaluation planned for independent compliance checks?
